If that slackening continues, retail visits should keep recovering over the next four weeks as more time is available for shopping and eating out outside commuting hours.

mechanism_narrative: When TRANSIT falls below its current weak level and remains there for a week, fewer trips to stations translate into fewer impulse retail stops nearby. That should push RETAIL_REC lower within one to two weeks because station-adjacent foot traffic is the immediate feeder for discretionary retail.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT falls further below -5 points week-on-week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises over the next 14 days after a further week-on-week drop in TRANSIT below -5.

mechanism_narrative: If GROCERY_PHARM keeps rising while PARKS stays suppressed, household errand time is being reallocated toward necessities rather than leisure. failure_condition: RETAIL_REC weakens over the next 28 days while GROCERY_PHARM continues to rise and PARKS remains below baseline.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp additional rise in RESIDENTIAL above its current level indicates renewed stay-at-home pressure, which directly suppresses discretionary outings and retail browsing. mechanism_narrative: A synchronized rebound in TRANSIT and WORKPLACES reduces the friction of going out for combined commuting and shopping trips. mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in PARKS relative to baseline reflects more leisure-oriented outings that compete with retail time. failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not fall in the next 7 days while PARKS continues to increase.

failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises over the next 14 days despite WORKPLACES improving while TRANSIT remains below its recent level.

mechanism_narrative: Under a reopening regime, the combination of high GROCERY_PHARM and improving TRANSIT should amplify neighborhood activity and pull discretionary spending back into malls and high streets. If transit losses narrow while grocery-pharmacy trips remain elevated, RETAIL_REC should increase over the next four weeks.
